skills_considered.reason: A complete local PMC XML was supplied; only linked supplements required retrieval.
The operator fixed the sequential reading order.
The four canonical scientific files were intentionally untouched.

group_assessment.weighting: The Aqeilan laboratory is a high-volume primary WWOX group. Model continuity does not remove the complete genetic-background confounding between Wwox and Trp53 mouse cohorts or turn same-group results into external replication.

field_density.note: The breast-cancer field is dense; the basal-like intersection is narrower, but direct causal interpretation remains limited by background and rare human deletion groups.

multihop.note: All 75 references were enumerated sequentially. PMID 27550453 is a direct WWOX-p53 cooperation source and was read next.

corpus_crossquery.query: Where do basal-like mammary, TP53 and WWOX mechanisms already occur, and what boundary does PMID 30082886 add?
corpus_crossquery.note: Post-reading audit found 13 file hits. The paper adds somatic mammary evidence but its central cross-model comparison remains strain-confounded.

retraction_check.result: Repository and indexed-record checks on 2026-08-10 found no retraction, expression of concern or correction.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: The local PMC JATS identifies PMCID PMC6079009 and contains a complete body, methods, captions, supplementary links and 75-reference list; all used surfaces are fingerprinted.

entries.proposition: The Wwox mammary line was backcrossed onto tumour-susceptible C3H/HeJ for seven rounds.
entries.snippet: Wwox ΔMGE mice (on B6/129 genetic background) 36 were back-crossed onto the C3H/HeJ mice (shortly named C3H), a mammary tumor-susceptible genetic background, for seven rounds (~99% purity) generating Wwox ΔMMTV .

entries.proposition: The Wwox-deleted cohort developed mammary tumours in 14 of 17 mice.
entries.snippet: mammary tumors with median latency of 270 days

entries.proposition: The authors explicitly require a C3H-facilitated second hit rather than WWOX deletion alone.
entries.snippet: Our findings suggest that WWOX deletion by itself might not be enough for BLBC development, and that a second hit facilitated in the C3H background, like perturbations in p53 signaling or locus, is required.

entries.proposition: The body does not claim worse survival from adding WWOX perturbation within TP53-perturbed patients.
entries.snippet: Furthermore, while TP53 perturbation was associated with poorer survival as expected (Fig. 4b ), genetic perturbation of WWOX was not associated with poorer survival of TP53-perturbed patients (Fig. 4b ).

entries.proposition: The human co-deletion result is driven by extremely small altered groups.
entries.snippet: Figure 4A prints 2 WWOX-deleted among 5 TP53-deleted tumors, 6 WWOX-deleted among 2047 tumors without TP53 deletion, and N = 2052.

entries.proposition: The survival panel supplies an omnibus test but no double-versus-TP53-only pairwise test.
entries.snippet: Figure 4B prints four survival curves and an overall P = 2E-4, but no pairwise statistic comparing TP53-perturbed/WWOX-WT with TP53-WWOX-perturbed patients.

entries.proposition: The supplementary rescue restores WWOX and reverses the knockout phenotype.
entries.snippet: Supplementary Figure S3 displays WWOX re-expression in KO cells with reduced colony formation and restored DNA-damage-response readouts relative to KO controls.
entries.anchor: Supplementary Figure S3, slide 4 rendered at measured 59.8-effective-PPI ceiling
